tour.title: Project Overview & Architecture Map
tour.description: Start with the project's own narrative. **README.md** introduces `xuan_common` as the shared Flutter base module for four divination sub-apps (奇门遁甲/七政四余/太乙神数/大六壬), highlighting the dual database, AI integration, and layout editor. **CLAUDE.md** is the primary architectural reference and the best cheat-sheet you will use for the rest of the tour — it lays out the Drift dual-DB, feature modules, AI integration, and the editor command pattern. Read these first so the code structure below matches the story the project tells about itself.

tour.title: Module Bootstrap & Public Surface
tour.description: Every consumer of `xuan_common` enters through these two files. **`lib/main.dart`** is the runnable demo entry: it initializes fonts, timezones, persistence stores, then mounts `MyApp` inside a MultiProvider wired with `AppDatabase` and ViewModels — a complete picture of which services the module needs at boot. **`lib/module.dart`** is the package's *public* barrel — the export list defines what downstream divination apps actually consume (painters, models, widgets, viewmodels, database, logger). Read these together to see both *how* the module starts and *what* it offers.
tour.languageLesson: Dart `library` barrel files (`module.dart`) re-export with `export 'src/foo.dart';` — this is the canonical way to expose a curated public API while keeping `lib/src/...` private. The `MultiProvider` in `main.dart` is the Provider package's idiom for composing many `ChangeNotifierProvider`s without nesting.

tour.title: Drift Dual-Database Layer
tour.description: `xuan_common` runs on two Drift-ORM databases. **`AppDatabase`** owns 21 tables and 19 DAOs covering divinations, panels, seekers, layout templates and audit records — it is the most fan-in heavy file in the entire codebase (44 incoming edges). **`tables.dart`** holds every table class definition and is the schema's source of truth. **`WorldInfoDatabase`** is the second DB — a separate read-only geography catalog (countries / states / cities / regions) used for birth-location lookups. Together they implement the *write-heavy app data + read-only reference data* split described in CLAUDE.md.
tour.languageLesson: Drift declares schema with Dart classes (e.g. `class Divinations extends Table`) and generates the typed query API via build_runner. The `@DriftDatabase(tables: [...], daos: [...])` annotation on `AppDatabase` is what wires tables + DAOs into a single generated implementation.

tour.title: Chinese Metaphysics Vocabulary — The Domain Enums
tour.description: Before any calculation makes sense, learn the *words*. These enums encode 2,000+ years of Chinese divination vocabulary into Dart's type system. **`enum_tian_gan.dart`** (天干, 10 Heavenly Stems) carries Yin-Yang polarity, Five Elements, Ten Gods, and 合化 relations. **`enum_di_zhi.dart`** (地支, 12 Earthly Branches) adds hidden stems, zodiac, month tokens. **`enum_jia_zi.dart`** is the 60-pair sexagenary cycle binding the two — the single most-imported file in the codebase (fan-in 47). **`enums.dart`** is the convenience barrel that re-exports the lot. Every feature module, model and widget downstream depends on this vocabulary.
tour.languageLesson: Dart's enhanced enums (since Dart 2.17) carry fields, constructors and methods — used here to attach `wuXing`, `yinYang`, and combination logic directly to each `TianGan` value instead of scattering switch-statements across the codebase.

tour.title: Domain Models & Calendar Helpers
tour.description: Built on the enum vocabulary, these are the *value objects* that flow through every layer. **`EightChars`** is the four-pillar 八字 value object (year/month/day/hour JiaZi + ten-gods accessors). **`Location`** composes precise coordinates with hierarchical address — the central type for birth location. **`solar_lunar_datetime_helper.dart`** is the cross-cutting bridge that ties Swiss Ephemeris (`sweph`), `tyme` and timezone packages together; it handles solar-term boundaries, mean/true solar time, DST, and three-yuan-nine-yun conversion — i.e. all the calendar math the engines lean on.

tour.title: Four-Pillars Engine — The Core of Divination
tour.description: The heart of every divination calculation. **`four_zhu_engine.dart`** combines pluggable `DayPillar` and `HourPillar` strategies and orchestrates `tyme` solar-time math — this is where birth datetime → 八字 happens. The four `strategies/*` files demonstrate the **Strategy pattern** the engine uses to swap between Zi-Ping fixed-hour, five-mouse-dun, and 23/00 boundary conventions. **`da_yun_calculator.dart`** sits on top of the engine to compute the sequence of decade pillars (大运) from birth — the gateway to luck-cycle features.
tour.languageLesson: The strategy pattern in Dart typically uses an `abstract class` (here `DayPillarStrategy` / `HourPillarStrategy`) with concrete subclasses selected at runtime — a clean alternative to large switch statements when divination conventions vary by school.

tour.title: Luck Cycles & Conception — liu_yun and tai_yuan
tour.description: Two feature modules built on top of the four-pillars engine. **liu_yun** computes 流年/流月/流日/流时 (yearly/monthly/daily/hourly luck): `yun_liu_service.dart` calls the DaYun calculator and produces UI-ready display models, surfaced via `yun_liu_view_model.dart` and the `liu_yun.dart` public barrel. **tai_yuan** computes 胎元 (conception pillar) using a `TaiYuanCalculatorFactory` that dispatches across multiple strategies — birthday count-back, day-master Yin-Yang, direct conception. Together they demonstrate the *feature module* convention CLAUDE.md describes: each business area is a self-contained folder with its own calculator, service, viewmodel and widgets.

tour.title: AI Domain — Persona, Context & Agent Tools
tour.description: `xuan_common` is AI-aware out of the box. The `domain/ai/` folder declares the contracts that decouple LLM integration from any specific provider. **`AiPersona`** models the virtual diviner (卦师). **`AiContext`** bundles module identity, user intention, and `AiEntity` payloads into the bridge object every AI call receives. **`AgentTool`** is the *Link B contract* — child divination modules expose their domain functions to the LLM as OpenAI/DeepSeek-style function declarations. **`AiAuditLog`** captures every chat/action/tool-call for security & debugging. `ai_service.dart` (services layer) is the abstract façade implementations plug into.

tour.title: The Editable Four-Zhu Card — The Big Editor
tour.description: The crown jewel of the UI: a fully drag-and-drop editable 八字 card. **`four_zhu_card_host.dart`** is the responsive top-level host that adapts the card to phone / tablet / desktop and wires DAOs, templates, market, theme dock. Inside lives **`editable_fourzhu_card_impl.dart`** — a massive StatefulWidget orchestrating drag-and-drop, sizing, theming, cell rendering, and ghost previews. The visual contract lives in **`editable_four_zhu_card_theme.dart`** (card/pillar/cell/typography sections with JSON serialization) backed by **`base_style_config.dart`** which defines the JSON-serializable Color/Offset/EdgeInsets/BoxShadow/BoxBorder primitives the whole theme system uses.
tour.languageLesson: Flutter `StatefulWidget` + `Draggable`/`DragTarget` form the standard drag-and-drop trio; the editable card uses `drag_payloads.dart` as a typed envelope so the `DragTarget<DragPayload>` constraint catches mismatched drops at compile time instead of via runtime casts.

tour.title: Style Editor & Command Pattern (Undo/Redo)
tour.description: Editing a card without undo/redo would be unforgivable. **`editor_command.dart`** defines `EditorCommand` (`execute` / `undo` / `canMergeWith`) and the `CommandHistory` stack — classic GoF Command pattern. **`template_commands.dart`** implements every layout-template mutation as a command (add/remove/reorder groups, pillars, rows, divider styling, group toggling). **`theme_commands.dart`** maps runtime theme tweaks (padding, fonts, row styles) back to the persistent `LayoutTemplate` and uses `canMergeWith` to coalesce consecutive slider updates into one undo step. The **`four_zhu_card_style_editor`** module is the UI face — the side-panel that drives all those commands.
tour.languageLesson: The Command pattern in Dart pairs naturally with `ChangeNotifier`: each command mutates state then the view-model notifies listeners. The `canMergeWith` hook is the key to good UX — without it every keystroke or slider tick becomes its own undo entry.

tour.title: MVVM Presentation Glue — ViewModels & Pages
tour.description: The link between business logic and the screen. **`four_zhu_editor_view_model.dart`** is the central ChangeNotifier (fan-in 20, fan-out 30) — it orchestrates template CRUD, the undo/redo command stack, gallery filtering and theme overlay. **`four_zhu_edit_page.dart`** is the page that wires DAOs, use-cases, repositories and view models into the editor workspace, complete with error/unsaved banners. **`editor_workspace.dart`** hosts the editable card itself plus the template gallery and hover-expand action menus. Together these show how the data layer (Step 3) and the card (Step 9) actually reach the user.
tour.languageLesson: Flutter MVVM with the Provider package: ViewModel extends `ChangeNotifier`, the View consumes it via `context.watch<T>()` (rebuilds on change) or `context.read<T>()` (event-only). The View never mutates state directly — every change goes through a ViewModel method, which is what makes commands reversible.

tour.title: Test Suite — Verifying the Whole Stack
tour.description: Final stop: where everything is validated. **`command_history_test.dart`** locks down the undo/redo stack, mergeability, and template/theme command composition (covers Step 10). **`four_zhu_editor_view_model_test.dart`** is the heaviest test — full lifecycle of the editor view-model including market-template installs (covers Steps 11 and 3). **`app_database_seed_templates_test.dart`** validates the dual-DB schema and template seeding (Step 3). **`boundary_end_of_month_year_test.dart`** is a focused unit test for the trickiest piece of Step 6 — solar-term and month-boundary edge cases in the four-pillars engine. Run these to confirm any change you make.
tour.languageLesson: Dart tests use the `test` (or `flutter_test`) package: `group('...', () { test('...', () { expect(actual, matcher); }); })`. Drift's in-memory database (`NativeDatabase.memory()`) is the canonical way to test DAO code without touching disk — fast, isolated, and parallel-safe.
